# Module `lune_ui_core::testing`

[API reference](../INDEX.md) / parent [`lune_ui_core`](index.md)

Fakes of the toolkit's seams, for tests in this crate and in apps.

- [`RecordingRenderer`](testing.md#struct.RecordingRenderer): the display-list seam's fake; records the draw calls a renderer
  issues for a [`Scene`](scene.md#struct.Scene), in the documented draw order.
- [`FakeText`](testing.md#struct.FakeText): the text seam's fake, deterministic sizes with no fonts; and
  [`text_system_contract`](testing.md#fn.text_system_contract), the properties every [`TextSystem`](text.md#trait.TextSystem)
  must have.
- [`NullMaterial`](testing.md#struct.NullMaterial): the material seam's fake, a backdrop with no OS glass; and
  [`backdrop_contract`](testing.md#fn.backdrop_contract), the properties every [`Backdrop`](backdrop.md#trait.Backdrop) must have.
- [`FakeImages`](testing.md#struct.FakeImages): the image seam's fake, a store that keeps sizes; and
  [`image_store_contract`](testing.md#fn.image_store_contract), the properties every [`ImageStore`](image.md#trait.ImageStore) must have.
- [`ScriptedInput`](testing.md#struct.ScriptedInput): the input seam's fake, a scripted window producing [`RawInput`](input.md#struct.RawInput)
  frames; and [`scripted_input_contract`](testing.md#fn.scripted_input_contract), the properties its frames must have.
- [`UiHarness`](testing.md#struct.UiHarness): a `Ui` test bench (store, fake text, default strings, scripted input); and
  [`disabled_violations`](testing.md#fn.disabled_violations), the nodes under a root that a disabled scope left enabled.
- [`fill_shapes`](testing.md#fn.fill_shapes) and [`fill_covers`](testing.md#fn.fill_covers): the bounds of each path-filled shape of a colour, such
  as a text selection, and whether one covers a point.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/testing/mod.rs:1`

<a id="struct.FakeText"></a>
### Struct `FakeText`

```rust
pub struct FakeText;
```

A deterministic [`TextSystem`](text.md#trait.TextSystem) with no fonts, for tests.

- key: `TextKey(spec.cache_key(scale))`, so it matches any real system's identity rule;
- width: the sum over runs of char count × size × 0.5 (logical px), so every char is half its
  run's size wide;
- lines break at `\n`, `\r\n` and a lone `\r` (the ending is not part of a line); with `wrap: Some(w)`,
  `w > 0` and a widest line above `w`, each line above `w` shows as `ceil(line width / w)` rows
  (at most one per char, the chars spread evenly over them) and the width is `w`; otherwise the
  width is the widest line's;
- height: rows × the first run's line height, or 17.0 with no runs (as the shaping cache gives
  an empty spec);
- queries: the caret and hit follow the half-size chars and the rows `prepare` counts, as
  `lines` lists them (a row's end is the next one's start, where the caret belongs to the later
  row, so `hit` right of a row answers its last char); `segments` groups combining marks U+0300 to U+036F, U+FE0F, U+200D and
  the skin tones U+1F3FB to U+1F3FF onto the char before them, a U+200D also joins the
  pictographic char after it, and `\r\n` is one cluster; a word is a run of clusters led by an
  alphanumeric char, a run of clusters led by whitespace, or any other single cluster.

Never panics.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/testing/text.rs:27`

<a id="struct.ScriptedInput"></a>
### Struct `ScriptedInput`

```rust
pub struct ScriptedInput {
    // some fields omitted
}
```

Builds a window's [`RawInput`](input.md#struct.RawInput) frames by hand. Size, scale, time, focus, pointer position and
modifiers persist across frames; [`ScriptedInput::end_frame`](testing.md#method.ScriptedInput.end_frame) takes the events and keeps the
state. It follows the same rules as the winit translator: positions are logical, the pointer
starts at (0, 0), the window starts unfocused, button and scroll events carry the pointer
position and modifiers current at that point, and a key press with printable text is followed
by a `Text` event.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/testing/input.rs:18`

## Functions

<a id="fn.backdrop_contract"></a>
### Function `backdrop_contract`

```rust
pub fn backdrop_contract(b: &mut dyn Backdrop) -> Result<(), String>
```

Checks the properties every [`Backdrop`](backdrop.md#trait.Backdrop) must have; the error names the first that fails.

- P1: `apply(Material::Opaque)` is Ok;
- P2: when `best_supported()` is `Opaque`, every glass material is an Err;
- P3: `apply(Material::Opaque)` twice in a row is Ok;
- P4: a `Custom` material that names no OS (both arms `None`) is an Err on every backdrop.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/testing/backdrop.rs:38`

<a id="fn.fill_shapes"></a>
### Function `fill_shapes`

```rust
pub fn fill_shapes(geometry: &LayerGeometry, color: Rgba) -> Vec<Rect>
```

The bounds of each filled shape of `color` (straight alpha, as a theme holds it) in
`geometry.fills`, in physical px, in drawn order: one per `Painter::fill_path`, `sector` or
`fill_joined` call, so one per joined text selection shape (`widgets::selection`). A shape's
bounds are its outline's, without the antialiasing fringe. Two shapes are told apart by their
layout in the list: a shape's interior triangles, then its fringe.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/testing/mod.rs:38`

<a id="fn.image_store_contract"></a>
### Function `image_store_contract`

```rust
pub fn image_store_contract<S: ImageStore>(
    store: &mut S,
    live: impl Fn(&S) -> usize,
    limit: Option<u32>,
) -> Result<(), String>
```

Checks the properties every [`ImageStore`](image.md#trait.ImageStore) must have; the error names the first that fails.
`live` reads how many pictures the store holds now. `limit` is the most a side may be when the
store has a small enough one to probe (pass `None` to skip P6).

- P1: a valid picture registers, and `live` counts it;
- P2: a buffer that is not `4 * width * height` bytes is refused with `BadLength` and changes
  nothing, also for an id that is registered;
- P3: registering an id again replaces the picture and frees the old one (`live` unchanged);
- P4: releasing frees the id (`live` drops), and releasing an unknown id does nothing;
- P5: an id registers again after its release;
- P6: a side above `limit` is refused with `TooLarge { limit }` and changes nothing.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/testing/images.rs:105`

<a id="fn.scripted_input_contract"></a>
### Function `scripted_input_contract`

```rust
pub fn scripted_input_contract(
    take: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut ScriptedInput) -> RawInput,
) -> Result<(), String>
```

Checks the properties of the input seam's fake; the error names the first that fails.
`take` ends a frame of the script it is given: [`ScriptedInput::end_frame`](testing.md#method.ScriptedInput.end_frame) is the real answer,
and a fake that only wraps or forwards it must pass the same suite.

- I1: size, scale, time and focus appear in the frame as set, and time passes as given (it
  does not advance by itself, and a later frame keeps it until it is set again);
- I2: events come out in the order they were added, within one frame and from frame to frame;
- I3: each event ends up in exactly one frame (the next frame starts empty), while size, scale,
  time, focus, pointer position and modifiers persist;
- I4: a button or scroll event carries the pointer position and modifiers current at that
  point of the script, not the ones at the end of the frame;
- I5: a key press with printable text is followed by one `Text` event; control characters are
  dropped and a press with nothing left emits none.

Source: `crates/lune-ui-core/src/testing/input.rs:240`

<a id="fn.text_system_contract"></a>
### Function `text_system_contract`

```rust
pub fn text_system_contract(ts: &mut dyn TextSystem) -> Result<(), String>
```

Checks the properties every [`TextSystem`](text.md#trait.TextSystem) must have; the error names the first that fails.

- P1: preparing the same spec at the same scale twice gives the same key and size;
- P2: the same spec at scales 1 and 2 gives different keys;
- P3: different text gives different keys;
- P4: `measure` equals `prepare`'s size;
- P5: an empty spec (no runs) has width 0 and a finite height ≥ 0;
- P6: "aa bb cc dd ee ff gg" at `Style::ui(13.0, …)` wrapped at 40 is at most 41 wide;
- P7: every size is finite and ≥ 0;
- P8: the queries on an empty spec and on empty text answer finite values (the caret at 0, one
  line) and a `pos` that is not finite hits 0;
- P9: an offset past the end clamps to the end, one inside a char to the char's start;
- P10: the caret at 0 has `x == 0`, and at the end of one unwrapped line it has exactly the
  width `prepare` returns, also after a cluster of several glyphs;
- P11: for a system that lays text out (width above 0), `hit` of the caret of each boundary of
  an ASCII line is that boundary;
- P12: on a three-line spec joined with `\n` and `\r\n` the lines start at the joined offsets, in
  order, top to bottom, and the caret of each start is on its line at the line's top; a final
  terminator opens one more, empty line;
- P13: `segments` of every [`SEGMENT_TABLE`](testing.md#constant.SEGMENT_TABLE) text is the table's boundaries, for both units;
- P14: `hit` keeps the column outside the lines: a point above the first line answers as that
  line at the same `x`, a point below the last answers as the last, left and right of a line
  are its first and last offset;
- P15: the queries and `prepare` agree on the lines, for hard and soft breaks and a final
  terminator: `measure`'s height is the last row's bottom, the rows stack with no gap and run in
  text order, the caret of each row's start is on that row, the caret at the end is on the last
  row, and `hit` at each row's left edge shows the caret of its start;
- P16: a line break is one break, whatever the rest of the text holds: the rows of a table of
  ASCII and non-ASCII texts are the table's byte ranges, and around each break the caret at and
  inside it is at the row's end and the caret after it at the next row's start;
- P17: along a row the caret never moves left as the offset grows, also through a run of spaces
  at a wrap;
- P18: on any row, `hit` of the caret of a grapheme boundary shows the same caret: that boundary,
  or another one at the same place, as a space dropped at a wrap and the glyph after it are;
- P19: the caret of every grapheme boundary is on the last row whose start is at or before it,
  the row `lines` gives it to;
- P20: `hit` on a row answers an offset of that row whose caret is on it, wherever the point is
  along the row: right of a soft-wrapped row that is not the next row's first offset;
- P21: on a row of left-to-right text, `hit` does not go backwards as `x` grows, in steps of a
  half pixel from left of the row to right of it, through a cluster of several glyphs too.

### Constant `SEGMENT_TABLE`

```rust
pub const SEGMENT_TABLE: &[SegmentCase];
```

Boundaries every [`TextSystem::segments`](text.md#tymethod.TextSystem.segments) must give. The expectations are worked out by hand;
the text cache's tests check them against the real UAX #29 implementation.
